description: Change of use from Class C3 (Single Family Dwellinghouse) to a 9-person Large HMO (Sui Generis), erection of a part single, part double storey rear extension, rear dormer, and 2 x front roof lights (part retrospective)
decision_conditions: The development, by virtue of the loss of the existing family dwelling, would conflict with the Borough's strategic housing goal of safeguarding 3-bedroom family dwellings and the proposed change of use to a Large HMO would be harmful to the character of the area. Consequently, the principle of development is considered to be unacceptable. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMH 1, DMH 2, DMH 5, DMHB 11 and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposed change of use of the property from a dwellinghouse (Use Class C3) to a large House in Multiple Occupation (Sui Generis) accommodating up to 9 unrelated occupants would result in an over-intensive form of residential occupation. By reason of the number of independently occupied bedrooms, the limited communal accommodation, and the materially different living patterns associated with 9 unrelated adults, the proposal would generate increased levels of noise, comings and goings, visitor activity, and use of outdoor amenity space, resulting in unacceptable harm to the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers. The submitted HMO Management Plan does not overcome the inherent land-use impacts arising from the scale and intensity of the proposed occupation. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies D3 and D13 of the London Plan (2021), Policies DMHD 1, DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), and Paragraph 135(f) of the National Planning Policy Frame

The development, by reason of the cumulative impact of the existing extensions has resulted in an excessively enlarged and overdeveloped form of development. Whilst certain elements of the development have been approved or established as lawful individually, the combined scale, bulk, massing and design of the extensions fail to remain subordinate to the original dwelling and appear visually dominant and incongruous within the street scene. The development therefore causes harm to the character and appearance of the host dwelling and the surrounding area, contrary to Policies D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One Strategic Policies (2012), and Policies DMHB 11, DMHB 12 and DMHD 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The proposed development, by reason of the inadequate quantity and quality of communal internal accommodation serving up to nine occupiers, would fail to provide sufficient shared living space to meet the day-to-day needs of future residents. The resulting over-reliance on private bedrooms for communal and recreational activities would lead to a poor standard of residential accommodation. Furthermore, the ground floor rear bedrooms would be positioned in direct relationship with the communal rear garden without the provision of adequate defensible space, resulting in poor levels of privacy for future occupiers. The proposal would therefore fail to provide satisfactory living conditions and a high standard of residential amenity for future occupants, contrary to Policies DMH 5, DMHB 11, DMHB 16 and DMHB 18 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 135(f) of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.

We have however been unable to seek solutions to problems arising from the application as the principal of the proposal is clearly contrary to our statutory policies and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.
